text:
anna: Heads-up — noticed spike in NAT ephemeral port exhaustion in us-west-2 after we flipped the DNS TTL to 5s. Metrics: NATGw 85% ports in use, connection resets rising.
infra-bot: Alert: natgw-usw2-1 ephemeral_ports_utilization=85% conn_resets=1240 period=5m
raj: ugh, did the DNS change cause more short-lived outbound connections? any logs showing DNS churn? :eyes:
jordan: yes, we saw a ton of repeated lookups to discovery.redwood.local from sidecars. Each lookup triggers new outbound TCP to DNS resolver then to external model hosts — lots of short lives.
lina: quick check — are pods using node-local-dns or cluster DNS? I thought we rolled node-local in staging but not prod.
anna: prod still on cluster coredns (no node-local). TTL 5s + no caching in sidecar = thundering DNS lookups.
raj: mitigation options: a) revert TTL b) enable node-local-dns c) add local caching to sidecar d) bump ephemeral port range on nodes or scale NATGW. Which is fastest?
jordan: fastest is revert TTL to 60s (canary first). Next fast: enable node-local-dns rollout (helm) but that needs rollout window. Scaling NATGW is slower and costly.
lina: also consider increasing ip_local_port_range on nodes: sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="15000 61000" but that only delays exhaustion if connection churn stays.
anna: logs snippet from one busy pod: ```connect to 10.0.0.2:53 -> resolved discovery.redwood.local -> connect to 52.14.23.8:443 -> SYN_SENT -> FIN, reason=RST```
raj: if SYNs are resetting at natgw, add keepalive or persistent connections in sidecar. Can we flip sidecar setting to pool connections for model fetches?
jordan: sidecar change is small: set HTTP2 pooled connections and enable connection reuse. Patch looks like: ```env: MODEL_CONN_POOL=1; MODEL_CONN_KEEPALIVE=60s``` Rollout in QA first.
lina: I'll schedule TTL revert and open PR for node-local-dns. Also we'll open infra ticket to request a temporary NATGW second elastic attachment for the AZ.
anna: thanks — I'll watch port utilization and post updates. /cc @raj @jordan
infra-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-0043 - NATGw port pressure — assigned to eng-infra oncall
raj: quick status — if port usage >90%, auto-signal to scale or failover AZ? We should add a runbook step. :fire_engine:
jordan: agreed. I'll add runbook snippet: "if ephemeral_ports_utilization > 90% then: 1) revert TTL, 2) enable node-local-dns canary on 10% nodes, 3) request NATGW burst capacity or open support case"
lina: PR for TTL revert: https://git.internal/redwood/dns-configs/pull/314 — deploying in 5m canary.
anna: canary looks stable so far (5m) — ports down to 60% on canary nodes. I'll update after 15m.
raj: perfect. thanks team.
